summary: Yinshun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes, National Taiwan Normal University, and Taisho University, learning under Taixu and Qingnian. He taught at Minnan, Wuchang, Fawang, Shandao Temple, and National Cheng Kung University.
Yirmiyahu Yovel (1935–2018) was a philosopher who was educated at Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (circa 1958–1968), and Princeton University (circa 1966–1968).
Yiu Wing Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong in 2013 under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv, Hanazono, and Kyoto universities under Ben-Ami Scharfstein and Sojo Hirano, and served as professor at the University of Haifa (~1978–2005).
Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Takatsugu Hayashi and served as an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

Yohei Kawajiri works in Indology and philosophy. He held appointments as a research associate and staff member at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013, 2022) and as a fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda (born 1954) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and later as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003, 2015).
Yoichi Kawada (born 1937) is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who served as director of the Institute of Oriental Philosophy (attested 2002, 2016).
Yong Hua is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014) under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries, he served as lopön at Menri and Triten Norbutse, and was a visiting scholar at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Sherab Ling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under teachers including Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and became abbot of Sherab Ling around 1998.
Yongshan He is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, as well as under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. After studying at Tsinghua and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Irving Babbitt, he held posts at Southeast, Nankai, National Central, and National Southwestern Associated universities, and Peking University.

Yongyu Chen specializes in Buddhist studies. Chen completed a BA at Cornell University, pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University, served as a professor at Joong-Ang Sangha University (attested 2015), and held an ArtTable Fellowship at Public Art Fund (2025).

Yonten Gyatso (1933–2002) was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he later served as research advisor for Tibetan Studies.

Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Kyoto University, he held academic positions at Kyoto University, Kobe Women's University, Bukkyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Bunkyo University.

Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) is an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Toho Kenkyukai, Toyo Bunko, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto, later serving at Komazawa as lecturer (1971) and professor (2001), with research at the University of Virginia (1985).

Yoshihiko Amino (1929–2004) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (circa 1947–1950), he held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1967–1980) and Kanagawa University (~1980–1995).
Yoshihiko Nasu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and held leadership roles at Kongojushinkai and Kongozyu (attested 2017).
